sourceAudit.criticalOrderingQuestion: Collecting stage commands does NOT change their effective ordering relative to other durable command types: (1) Reconstruct already canonicalizes the list (repositories, running runs, terminals, units, stages) - it is never chronological; (2) stage rows exist only for running runs (Apply folds them on complete and removes them on terminal run), so groups always belong to running runs and cannot mix publication generations; (3) stage processing remains strictly between published-unit restoration (step 3) and terminal-history restoration (step 5); (4) per-RunKey staged state is independent (ApplyStagedChanges/ApplyStagedOccurrences), so group processing order cannot affect outcomes; (5) within a group the durable command order is preserved with last-command-wins per stage identity, reproducing live bookkeeping end states; (6) the live mutation path (StageIndexUnitAsync/StageIndexUnitDeletionAsync/ApplyCommandAsync/MutateAsync) is byte-identical to pre-R2.
sourceAudit.acceptRefuseEquivalence: Pre-R2, the last command of each contiguous group validated the complete set for that run; post-R2 the group validation runs over the same final set. Accept/refuse sets are therefore identical except for the intended removal of order-dependent intermediate refusals. Observable difference: staged graph failures now report 'The restored staged graph is invalid.' instead of the per-command message; error codes are the same vocabulary.
